name: Virial thermostat: stars heat up as they lose energy
summary: For a star in hydrostatic equilibrium the virial theorem gives total energy E=−K, so radiating energy away makes it contract and heat up (Kelvin–Helmholtz contraction). The same negative heat capacity keeps nuclear burning self-regulating: excess energy expands and cools the core.

name: Saha equation and cosmic recombination
summary: Chemical equilibrium μ_p+μ_e=μ_H between ideal gases gives the Saha equation. Photons outnumber baryons by 1/η≈1.6×10⁹, so hydrogen only recombines near k_BT≈0.3 eV, far below the 13.6 eV binding energy, and this sets the last-scattering surface.

name: Metastable and coexisting phases as dark-matter detectors
summary: Bubble chambers such as PICO keep a fluorocarbon superheated, as a metastable liquid. A nuclear recoil that deposits enough energy inside the critical radius nucleates a bubble (Seitz theory), and the threshold is tuned so electron recoils do not. Dual-phase xenon TPCs run at liquid–vapour coexistence so that drifted electrons are pulled into the gas, where they produce the S2 signal.

name: Clausius–Clapeyron runaway greenhouse sets the HZ inner edge
summary: Water-vapour pressure rises exponentially with temperature, so warming adds more greenhouse gas. Once the atmosphere is mostly steam, outgoing thermal radiation saturates near 280 W m⁻² (the Simpson–Nakajima limit) and the oceans evaporate. This defines the inner edge of the habitable zone.
sources: Kasting, Whitmire & Reynolds (1993). "Habitable Zones around Main Sequence Stars". *Icarus* 101, 108. [doi:10.1006/icar.1993.1010](https://doi.org/10.1006/icar.1993.1010)

name: Condensation curves and equilibrium chemistry in exoplanets
summary: Clouds form where a species' partial pressure meets its Clausius–Clapeyron saturation curve along the atmosphere's pressure–temperature profile: silicate and iron clouds on hot giants, KCl and Na₂S on cooler ones. Baseline compositions come from minimizing the Gibbs free energy. JWST spectra are read as departures from that baseline caused by vertical quenching and photochemistry.

name: White-dwarf crystallization and phase separation
summary: The core of a cooling white dwarf is a Coulomb plasma that freezes when the coupling Γ reaches about 175. Latent heat, plus oxygen sinking as the carbon–oxygen mixture phase-separates (a binary-mixture phase diagram), slows the cooling. Gaia sees this as a pile-up in the white-dwarf cooling sequence.

name: Adiabatic gradient, Γ₁ and stellar stability
summary: Stellar stability criteria are thermodynamic response functions. Convection starts when the radiative gradient exceeds ∇_ad (Schwarzschild criterion), and partial ionization lowers both ∇_ad and Γ₁. A star is dynamically unstable if its pressure-weighted Γ₁ drops below 4/3, and helioseismology measures Γ₁ inside the Sun to test the equation of state.

name: Γ₁<4/3 instabilities: core collapse and pair instability
summary: Some processes absorb energy without raising the pressure: iron photodisintegration and electron capture in collapsing cores, and electron–positron pair creation in very massive oxygen cores. They push Γ₁ below 4/3 and trigger collapse. Pair instability produces (pulsational) pair-instability supernovae and a predicted black-hole mass gap.
sources: Woosley, Heger & Weaver (2002). "The evolution and explosion of massive stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1015. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015)

name: Friends-of-friends halos and cosmic-web percolation
summary: The friends-of-friends halo finder links particles closer than b≈0.2 times the mean separation, so its halos are continuum-percolation clusters. Percolation statistics of over- and underdense regions were also an early quantitative test of the cosmic web's connected, filamentary topology.

name: Reionization as percolation of ionized bubbles
summary: Ionized regions around early galaxies grow and merge until they form a spanning cluster. Simulations and upcoming 21-cm maps are interpreted by treating this overlap phase as a percolation transition, using cluster-size and topology statistics.

name: Degenerate-matter equation of state for compact stars
summary: Counting states of indistinguishable fermions in the grand-canonical ensemble gives a pressure that survives at T=0; this equation of state, with Sommerfeld finite-temperature and ionic heat-capacity corrections, sets white-dwarf structure and cooling ages.

name: 21-cm spin temperature as a two-level Boltzmann ratio
summary: The populations of hydrogen's two hyperfine levels define a spin temperature through the Boltzmann factor. T_s is a weighted mean of the CMB, gas-kinetic and Lyman-α colour temperatures (Wouthuysen–Field coupling). The 21-cm signal appears in absorption when T_s is below T_CMB and in emission when it is above.

name: Negative heat capacity and gravothermal catastrophe in clusters
summary: The virial theorem gives self-gravitating systems a negative heat capacity, which the canonical ensemble cannot represent (ensembles become inequivalent). A core that loses heat to its halo contracts and gets hotter, so isothermal spheres are unstable once the centre-to-edge density ratio exceeds 709. Globular clusters therefore undergo core collapse, which binary heating halts.

name: Entropic/emergent gravity as a MOND-like alternative
summary: Verlinde proposed that gravity is an entropic force arising from information on holographic screens. He later proposed that de Sitter entropy adds an 'apparent dark matter' force that scales like MOND, with a₀~cH₀. The idea is speculative and contested.
breaks: It has no accepted derivation from microphysics, and key steps assume Newton's law. Its galaxy-scale predictions are under strain from dwarf-galaxy, cluster and Solar System tests.

name: Lynden-Bell violent relaxation as maximum-entropy statistics
summary: Lynden-Bell maximized the coarse-grained entropy of a collisionless system whose fine-grained phase-space density is conserved. That incompressibility acts like an exclusion principle and gives a Fermi–Dirac-like distribution. It explains why rapid collapse gives every star the same velocity dispersion regardless of mass.
breaks: Relaxation stops before it is complete as the potential settles. The predicted equilibria have infinite mass, and simulated (NFW-like) halos do not follow Lynden-Bell's distribution.

name: CMB as a Bose–Einstein photon gas
summary: The CMB is the most precisely measured Planck spectrum (FIRAS, T0=2.7255 K). Expansion redshifts frequency and temperature together, so the Bose–Einstein form survives. Late energy release would leave a chemical-potential (μ) distortion, now bounded at |μ|<9×10⁻⁵.
sources: Mather et al. (1994). "Measurement of the cosmic microwave background spectrum by the COBE FIRAS instrument". *Astrophys. J.* 420, 439. [doi:10.1086/173574](https://doi.org/10.1086/173574)

name: Thermal history: g_*, entropy conservation, relic neutrinos
summary: In the radiation era the universe is a quantum ideal gas of relativistic species. Energy and entropy densities count boson degrees of freedom, with fermions weighted by 7/8, and comoving entropy is conserved. Electron–positron annihilation heats photons but not the already decoupled neutrinos, giving T_ν/T_γ=(4/11)^{1/3} and N_eff≈3.044.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: Fuzzy dark matter as a degenerate Bose field
summary: Ultralight bosons (m~10⁻²² eV) have such large occupation numbers that they behave as a classical wave obeying the Schrödinger–Poisson equations. Their kiloparsec de Broglie wavelengths form solitonic, condensate-like cores, and gravitational relaxation can condense Bose stars. Claims that all axion dark matter forms one coherent BEC are disputed.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)

name: Fermi degeneracy pressure and the Chandrasekhar limit
summary: Electron degeneracy pressure P∝n^{5/3} softens to P∝n^{4/3} once electrons are relativistic. An n=3 polytrope then has a single allowed mass, the Chandrasekhar limit. The same Fermi-gas physics for neutrons, plus nuclear forces, sets the maximum mass of neutron stars.
sources: Chandrasekhar (1931). "The Maximum Mass of Ideal White Dwarfs". *Astrophys. J.* 74, 81. [doi:10.1086/143324](https://doi.org/10.1086/143324)
Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)

name: Degenerate cores and the helium flash
summary: In low-mass red giants the helium core is electron-degenerate, so its pressure barely depends on temperature. When helium ignites, the core heats without expanding, which defeats the virial thermostat, and the runaway helium flash continues until degeneracy is lifted. At the other extreme, blackbody radiation pressure dominates in massive stars.

name: Adhesion model: Zel'dovich flow as Burgers/KPZ
summary: Adding a small viscosity to the Zel'dovich approximation gives the Burgers equation for the comoving velocity, which a Cole–Hopf transform linearizes. Written for the velocity potential it is the noiseless KPZ equation, and its shocks reproduce the sheets, filaments and nodes of the cosmic web.

breaks: The viscosity is artificial. Matter sticks inside shocks, so there is no shell crossing or virialization within halos, and the randomness comes from initial conditions rather than from KPZ's noise.
sources: Kardar, Parisi & Zhang (1986). "Dynamic Scaling of Growing Interfaces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 56, 889. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889)

name: Solar flares as self-organized-criticality avalanches
summary: Flare energies follow a power law across many decades. Lu and Hamilton modelled the coronal magnetic field as a slowly driven sandpile whose reconnection avalanches reproduce that distribution, which made flares a leading astrophysical example of self-organized criticality.
breaks: Waiting-time statistics show memory and clustering that simple SOC does not predict, and the power-law index varies. A power law alone does not prove criticality, and the underlying physics is MHD reconnection.

name: Boltzmann hierarchy, Silk damping, non-equilibrium recombination
summary: CMB anisotropies come from solving the linearized photon Boltzmann equation with a Thomson collision term (the multipole hierarchy in CAMB/CLASS). The photons' finite mean free path lets the photon–baryon fluid diffuse, which erases the small-scale peaks (Silk damping). Peebles' rate equation shows that recombination lags behind Saha equilibrium.

name: SIDM halos as a conducting gas, then gravothermal collapse
summary: With σ/m~1 cm² g⁻¹, dark-matter self-scattering conducts heat like a dilute gas. It first builds an isothermal core, which addresses the cusp–core problem. Because the core has negative heat capacity, it can then undergo gravothermal collapse as globular clusters do, a process now invoked for unusually dense subhalos.
sources: Tulin & Yu (2018). "Dark matter self-interactions and small scale structure". *Phys. Rep.* 730, 1. [arXiv:1705.02358](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02358)

name: Thermal freeze-out sets the relic annihilation cross-section
summary: Integrating the Boltzmann equation over momenta gives a rate equation for the dark-matter number density. Annihilations freeze out once n⟨σv⟩ falls below H, at m/T≈20–25. Matching the observed Ω_DM fixes the 'thermal' ⟨σv⟩≈3×10⁻²⁶ cm³ s⁻¹ that gamma-ray searches in dwarf galaxies aim to test.
map: \dot n+3Hn=-\langle\sigma v\rangle(n^2-n_{\rm eq}^2),\ \Omega h^2\approx\frac{3\times10^{-27}\,{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}}{\langle\sigma v\rangle}

name: Collisionless Boltzmann and Jeans equations for the Galaxy
summary: Two-body relaxation times are far longer than the Galaxy's age, so stars obey the collisionless Boltzmann (Vlasov) equation. Its velocity moments, the Jeans equations, turn Gaia kinematics into a measurement of the local dark-matter density. The Gaia phase spiral is a collisionless system caught partway through phase mixing.
map: \partial_tf+\mathbf v\cdot\nabla f-\nabla\Phi\cdot\partial_{\mathbf v}f=0,\ t_{\rm relax}\approx\frac{N}{8\ln N}t_{\rm cross}
breaks: There is no collision term and so no H-theorem: the system relaxes by phase mixing and violent relaxation, not toward a Maxwellian.

name: Neutrino trapping and diffusion in core collapse
summary: Above about 10¹² g cm⁻³ the neutrino mean free path (∝E_ν⁻²) is far smaller than the core, so neutrinos are trapped. They leak out by diffusion from a neutrinosphere over about 10 s, with nearly Fermi–Dirac spectra. Supernova simulations solve the Boltzmann transport equation for them, and the ~13 s neutrino burst from SN 1987A confirmed the timescale.

name: Gamow peak: Maxwellian tail times tunnelling
summary: A thermonuclear rate is the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution multiplied by the Coulomb-tunnelling probability. The product peaks at the Gamow energy, about 6 keV for the pp reaction in the solar core where k_BT≈1.35 keV. The resulting steep temperature dependence, for example a ⁸B neutrino flux ∝T_c^{~24}, makes solar neutrinos a sensitive thermometer of the core.

name: Stochastic inflation: inflaton Langevin dynamics
summary: Averaged over a Hubble patch, the inflaton gets a random kick of size H/2π per e-fold from modes crossing the horizon. It therefore obeys a Langevin equation, and its probability distribution a Fokker–Planck equation. This underlies eternal inflation and the first-passage (stochastic-δN) predictions of non-Gaussian tails that matter for primordial black holes.

name: Excursion sets: halo mass function as first passage
summary: Smoothing the linear density field on ever smaller scales makes δ perform a random walk in the variance S=σ²(M). The halo mass function is the distribution of first crossings of the collapse barrier δ_c≈1.686, which reproduces Press–Schechter including its ad hoc factor of 2.
breaks: The walk is Markovian only for a sharp-k filter. Realistic filters and ellipsoidal collapse need non-Markovian corrections and moving barriers.

name: Kompaneets equation and the Sunyaev–Zel'dovich effect
summary: Repeated Compton scattering off Maxwellian electrons makes photons diffuse in frequency according to a Fokker–Planck equation, the Kompaneets equation. Its n² stimulated-emission term makes the steady state a Bose–Einstein distribution. In hot cluster gas it shifts CMB photons to higher frequency, producing the thermal SZ y-distortion used to find clusters.

name: Diffusive shock acceleration as a random walk with escape
summary: Charged particles scattered by magnetic turbulence random-walk back and forth across a shock. Each crossing cycle gives a fixed fractional energy gain, and each cycle carries a fixed probability of escaping downstream. The competition produces a power law, E⁻² for a strong shock; energy-dependent diffusion through the Galaxy then steepens it to the observed ~E⁻²·⁷.
sources: Fermi (1949). "On the Origin of the Cosmic Radiation". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1169. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1169](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1169)
Bell (1978). "The acceleration of cosmic rays in shock fronts – I". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 182, 147. [doi:10.1093/mnras/182.2.147](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/182.2.147)

name: Dust coagulation: Smoluchowski kinetics and Brownian growth
summary: Grain growth in protoplanetary disks is modelled with the Smoluchowski coagulation equation. Collision kernels come from Brownian motion for small grains and from turbulence and drift for larger ones. Gas drag in the Epstein (kinetic) regime sets the stopping time and Stokes number, which control settling, radial drift and the bouncing and fragmentation barriers.

name: Fokker–Planck stellar dynamics: relaxation, friction, evaporation
summary: Chandrasekhar treated the cumulative effect of weak stellar encounters as Brownian motion: a Fokker–Planck equation with a drag term (dynamical friction) and a velocity-diffusion term. In star clusters this drives mass segregation and the evaporation of stars scattered above the escape speed, about 0.7% of a Maxwellian per relaxation time.

name: Radiative diffusion as a photon random walk
summary: Inside a star a photon travels only up to about a centimetre before it is scattered or absorbed, so energy moves by diffusion. Fick's law with a Rosseland-mean opacity gives the radiative temperature gradient. Escaping the solar core takes 10⁴–10⁵ yr, compared with R/c≈2 s for a straight path.

name: Stochastically excited p-modes as noise-driven oscillators
summary: Solar acoustic modes are damped and also driven by random forcing from convection near the surface. Each behaves like a Langevin oscillator whose power spectrum is a Lorentzian with a linewidth set by the damping rate. This model is the basis of mode fitting in helioseismology and in asteroseismology of solar-like stars.
sources: Christensen-Dalsgaard (2002). "Helioseismology". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1073. [arXiv:astro-ph/0207403](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0207403)

name: Kibble–Zurek defect formation and the monopole problem
summary: When a symmetry breaks, causally disconnected regions pick independent vacua, leaving at least one defect per correlation volume; Zurek fixed the frozen correlation length using critical exponents. GUT monopoles made this way would overclose the universe, a key motivation for inflation. The scaling has been tested in superfluid helium, liquid crystals and cold atoms.
sources: Linde (1982). "A new inflationary universe scenario: A possible solution of the horizon, flatness, homogeneity, isotropy and primordial monopole problems". *Phys. Lett. B* 108, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(82)91219-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(82)91219-9)

name: Old inflation as a supercooled first-order transition
summary: Guth's inflation began as supercooling of a GUT phase transition. A Landau-type finite-temperature potential with a metastable false vacuum drives exponential expansion, which bubble nucleation was meant to end. The bubbles never percolate, so 'new' slow-roll inflation replaced the scenario.
sources: Guth (1981). "Inflationary universe: A possible solution to the horizon and flatness problems". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 347. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347)

Linde (1982). "A new inflationary universe scenario: A possible solution of the horizon, flatness, homogeneity, isotropy and primordial monopole problems". *Phys. Lett. B* 108, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(82)91219-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(82)91219-9)

name: Effective field theory of large-scale structure
summary: Integrating out the non-linear short-scale modes leaves an effective fluid. Its stress tensor has cutoff-dependent coefficients, such as the sound speed c_s², fixed by matching, exactly as in Wilsonian renormalization. Renormalized and time-RG perturbation theories resum loops to push predictions to mildly non-linear scales.

name: Atom interferometry constrains screened dark energy
summary: Atoms in a high vacuum are unscreened test masses; interferometers near a source mass bound chameleon-type dark-energy forces.
sources: Hamilton et al. (2015). "Atom-interferometry constraints on dark energy". *Science* 349, 849. [arXiv:1502.03888](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03888)

name: Clock networks as dark-matter detectors
summary: Networks of atomic clocks and magnetometers could detect transient frequency shifts from passing topological-defect dark matter, or oscillations from ultralight fields.
sources: Derevianko & Pospelov (2014). "Hunting for topological dark matter with atomic clocks". *Nature Phys.* 10, 933. [arXiv:1311.1244](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1244)
Arvanitaki, Huang & Van Tilburg (2015). "Searching for dilaton dark matter with atomic clocks". *Phys. Rev. D* 91, 015015. [arXiv:1405.2925](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2925)

name: Astrocombs calibrate radial-velocity planet searches
summary: Optical frequency combs, developed for clock metrology, give spectrographs absolute, evenly spaced calibration lines for cm/s radial-velocity precision needed for Earth analogues.
sources: Steinmetz et al. (2008). "Laser Frequency Combs for Astronomical Observations". *Science* 321, 1335. [doi:10.1126/science.1161030](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1161030)
Udem, Holzwarth & Hänsch (2002). "Optical frequency metrology". *Nature* 416, 233. [doi:10.1038/416233a](https://doi.org/10.1038/416233a)

name: Quasar absorption tests of varying alpha
summary: Relative wavelengths of metal absorption lines in quasar spectra, with laboratory sensitivity coefficients, constrain cosmic variation of the fine-structure constant; reported variations remain contested.
sources: Webb et al. (1999). "Search for Time Variation of the Fine Structure Constant". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 82, 884. [arXiv:astro-ph/9803165](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9803165)

name: Hydrogen atomic physics sets recombination
summary: Recombination is delayed beyond Saha equilibrium because Lyman-alpha photons are trapped; the 2s-1s two-photon decay and Lyman-alpha redshifting control the last-scattering surface and thus the CMB acoustic scale.
sources: Peebles (1968). "Recombination of the Primeval Plasma". *Astrophys. J.* 153, 1. [doi:10.1086/149628](https://doi.org/10.1086/149628)

name: 21-cm rotation curves trace dark halos
summary: Neutral-hydrogen 21-cm emission extends rotation curves far beyond stellar disks, where flat curves give the cleanest galactic evidence for dark matter.

name: Highly charged ion spectroscopy of cluster gas
summary: X-ray lines of He- and H-like iron give temperature, abundance and turbulent velocity of intracluster gas; Hitomi's resolved Fe XXV lines measured low turbulence in Perseus.
sources: Hitomi Collaboration (2016). "The quiescent intracluster medium in the core of the Perseus cluster". *Nature* 535, 117. [arXiv:1607.04487](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04487)

name: 21-cm hyperfine line and Lyman-alpha probe reionization
summary: The hydrogen hyperfine transition, its spin temperature set by collisions and Lyman-alpha pumping (Wouthuysen-Field), maps neutral gas at cosmic dawn; Gunn-Peterson Lyman-alpha absorption marks the end of reionization.
sources: Furlanetto, Oh & Briggs (2006). "Cosmology at low frequencies: The 21 cm transition and the high-redshift Universe". *Phys. Rep.* 433, 181. [arXiv:astro-ph/0608032](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0608032)
Gunn & Peterson (1965). "On the Density of Neutral Hydrogen in Intergalactic Space". *Astrophys. J.* 142, 1633. [doi:10.1086/148444](https://doi.org/10.1086/148444)

name: Lanthanide atomic data for kilonova spectra
summary: Kilonova light curves and spectra depend on the dense line forests of lanthanides and on identified features such as Sr II, requiring atomic-structure calculations of open f-shell ions.
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [arXiv:1710.05463](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05463)
Watson et al. (2019). "Identification of strontium in the merger of two neutron stars". *Nature* 574, 497. [arXiv:1910.10510](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10510)

name: Line lists for exoplanet atmosphere spectra
summary: Interpreting transmission and emission spectra needs ro-vibrational line lists of H2O, CH4, CO2 and metal atoms computed from molecular quantum mechanics.
sources: Tennyson & Yurchenko (2012). "ExoMol: molecular line lists for exoplanet and other atmospheres". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 425, 21. [arXiv:1204.0124](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.0124)

name: Atomic opacities and the solar abundance problem
summary: Stellar interiors depend on computed atomic opacities; measured iron opacity at solar-interior conditions exceeds theory, a candidate resolution of the mismatch between helioseismology and low solar metal abundances.
sources: Bailey et al. (2015). "A higher-than-predicted measurement of iron opacity at solar interior temperatures". *Nature* 517, 56. [doi:10.1038/nature14048](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14048)

name: Fuzzy dark matter as a cosmic matter wave
summary: Ultralight bosonic dark matter obeys the Schrodinger-Poisson system, a Gross-Pitaevskii equation with self-gravity; galaxy halos develop solitonic cores and granular interference like condensates.
breaks: Interaction is long-range self-gravity rather than contact scattering; occupation is classical and not reached by thermal condensation; no trap or superfluid flow measurement.
sources: Hu, Barkana & Gruzinov (2000). "Fuzzy Cold Dark Matter: The Wave Properties of Ultralight Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 85, 1158. [arXiv:astro-ph/0003365](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0003365)
Schive, Chiueh & Broadhurst (2014). "Cosmic structure as the quantum interference of a coherent dark wave". *Nature Phys.* 10, 496. [arXiv:1406.6586](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.6586)

name: Fermi pressure from trapped atoms to white dwarfs
summary: Degeneracy pressure measured in trapped Fermi gases is the same Pauli effect that supports white dwarfs and neutron stars against gravity.
sources: Truscott et al. (2001). "Observation of Fermi Pressure in a Gas of Trapped Atoms". *Science* 291, 2570. [doi:10.1126/science.1059318](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1059318)

name: Superfluid vortices and pulsar glitches
summary: Neutron-star interiors are superfluid; rotation is carried by quantized vortices whose sudden unpinning from the crust is the leading explanation of pulsar glitches, the physics of vortex lattices in rotating BECs.
sources: Anderson & Itoh (1975). "Pulsar glitches and restlessness as a hard superfluidity phenomenon". *Nature* 256, 25. [doi:10.1038/256025a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/256025a0)

name: Cold molecular collisions and astrochemistry
summary: Interstellar chemistry at 10-100 K proceeds by barrierless ion-molecule reactions and tunnelling, the same low-temperature collision physics that cold-molecule experiments resolve state by state.
sources: Herbst & Klemperer (1973). "The Formation and Depletion of Molecules in Dense Interstellar Clouds". *Astrophys. J.* 185, 505. [doi:10.1086/152436](https://doi.org/10.1086/152436)

name: Cosmological Bell inequalities
summary: Bell-type observables built from primordial correlators could in principle reveal the quantum origin of structure, though decaying modes make realistic tests extremely hard.
sources: Maldacena (2016). "A model with cosmological Bell inequalities". *Fortsch. Phys.* 64, 10. [arXiv:1508.01082](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01082)

name: Quasars choose settings in cosmic Bell tests
summary: Light from high-redshift quasars emitted billions of years ago set measurement bases in a Bell test, pushing any freedom-of-choice loophole back to the early universe.
sources: Rauch et al. (2018). "Cosmic Bell Test Using Random Measurement Settings from High-Redshift Quasars". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 080403. [arXiv:1808.05966](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05966)

name: Quantum-to-classical transition of cosmic fluctuations
summary: Large squeezing makes primordial fluctuations effectively classical stochastic fields, and environmental decoherence selects field amplitude as pointer basis; whether a quantum signature survives is debated.
sources: Polarski & Starobinsky (1996). "Semiclassicality and decoherence of cosmological perturbations". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 13, 377. [arXiv:gr-qc/9504030](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9504030)

name: Density-matrix kinetics of relic neutrinos
summary: Neutrino decoupling with oscillations and collisions is computed with matrix-valued quantum kinetic equations, giving N_eff = 3.044 used in CMB fits.
sources: Sigl & Raffelt (1993). "General kinetic description of relativistic mixed neutrinos". *Nucl. Phys. B* 406, 423. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(93)90175-O](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(93)90175-O)

name: Many-body entanglement in collective neutrino oscillations
summary: Neutrino-neutrino forward scattering in supernovae makes flavour evolution an interacting spin model; quantum-information tools quantify entanglement beyond mean-field treatments.
sources: Cervia, Patwardhan, Balantekin, Coppersmith & Johnson (2019). "Entanglement and collective flavor oscillations in a dense neutrino gas". *Phys. Rev. D* 100, 083001. [arXiv:1908.03511](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03511)

name: WKB asymptotics of solar oscillations
summary: High-order p-mode frequencies follow from JWKB analysis of the wave equation in the solar cavity, giving the large-separation formula used to invert sound speed.
sources: Tassoul (1980). "Asymptotic approximations for stellar nonradial pulsations". *Astrophys. J. Suppl.* 43, 469. [doi:10.1086/190678](https://doi.org/10.1086/190678)

name: Bounce instantons and false-vacuum decay
summary: The Euclidean bounce that computes tunnelling rates in quantum mechanics gives bubble nucleation in field theory and gravity, central to old and eternal inflation and vacuum stability.
sources: Coleman (1977). "Fate of the false vacuum: Semiclassical theory". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2929. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2929](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2929)
Coleman & De Luccia (1980). "Gravitational effects on and of vacuum decay". *Phys. Rev. D* 21, 3305. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.21.3305](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.21.3305)

name: Partial-wave cross sections of self-interacting dark matter
summary: Velocity-dependent self-interaction cross sections for Yukawa potentials are computed by partial-wave and Born methods; resonant and classical regimes control halo cores.
sources: Tulin, Yu & Zurek (2013). "Beyond Collisionless Dark Matter: Particle Physics Dynamics for Dark Matter Halo Structure". *Phys. Rev. D* 87, 115007. [arXiv:1302.3898](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3898)

name: Sommerfeld enhancement of dark-matter annihilation
summary: Slow dark-matter particles exchanging a light mediator have enhanced annihilation, the wavefunction-at-origin factor of Coulomb or Yukawa scattering, with resonances from near-threshold bound states.
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Finkbeiner, Slatyer & Weiner (2009). "A Theory of Dark Matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 79, 015014. [arXiv:0810.0713](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.0713)

name: Mechanical quantum sensors for dark matter
summary: Levitated and clamped mechanical sensors operated near the quantum limit can detect impulses or oscillating forces from heavy or ultralight dark matter.
sources: Carney et al. (2021). "Mechanical quantum sensing in the search for dark matter". *Quantum Sci. Technol.* 6, 024002. [arXiv:2008.06074](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06074)

name: Zero-point energy and the cosmological-constant problem
summary: Summing field-mode zero-point energies to a high cutoff predicts a vacuum energy far above the observed dark-energy density; the Casimir effect does not settle the issue because it measures energy differences.
breaks: Casimir forces arise from charge fluctuations and do not measure absolute vacuum energy; renormalization makes the naive cutoff estimate unphysical.
sources: Weinberg (1989). "The cosmological constant problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 61, 1. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1)
Jaffe (2005). "The Casimir effect and the quantum vacuum". *Phys. Rev. D* 72, 021301. [arXiv:hep-th/0503158](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0503158)

name: Intensity interferometry from stars to quantum optics
summary: Hanbury Brown and Twiss measured stellar diameters from intensity correlations; explaining the photon bunching behind the effect led Glauber to the quantum theory of optical coherence.
sources: Hanbury Brown & Twiss (1956). "A Test of a New Type of Stellar Interferometer on Sirius". *Nature* 178, 1046. [doi:10.1038/1781046a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/1781046a0)
Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)

name: Superconducting photon sensors for sub-GeV dark matter
summary: SNSPDs and transition-edge sensors developed for single-photon counting have meV thresholds, letting them detect electron recoils or absorption from light dark matter.
sources: Hochberg et al. (2019). "Detecting Sub-GeV Dark Matter with Superconducting Nanowires". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 123, 151802. [arXiv:1903.05101](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05101)

name: Primordial perturbations are squeezed states
summary: Inflation stretches vacuum fluctuations into extremely squeezed two-mode states of opposite-momentum modes; the growing mode's phase coherence underlies CMB acoustic peaks.
sources: Grishchuk & Sidorov (1990). "Squeezed quantum states of relic gravitons and primordial density fluctuations". *Phys. Rev. D* 42, 3413. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.42.3413](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.42.3413)
Albrecht, Ferreira, Joyce & Prokopec (1994). "Inflation and squeezed quantum states". *Phys. Rev. D* 50, 4807. [arXiv:astro-ph/9303001](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9303001)

name: Spinning black holes power AGN jets
summary: AGN engines are accreting Kerr black holes (Lynden-Bell 1969). In the Blandford–Znajek process, an electromagnetic version of the Penrose process, magnetic field lines threading the frame-dragged horizon extract its rotational energy and launch relativistic jets.
sources: Lynden-Bell (1969). "Galactic Nuclei as Collapsed Old Quasars". *Nature* 223, 690. [doi:10.1038/223690a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/223690a0)

name: Stellar-mass black holes as end states of collapse
summary: Above the maximum neutron-star mass (~2.2–2.3 M_sun) no pressure can halt collapse, so heavy stellar cores become Kerr black holes. X-ray binaries such as Cyg X-1 are where the GR geometry meets measured masses, spins inferred from the ISCO, and the lower mass gap at 2–5 M_sun.

name: Black-hole shadow as extreme gravitational lensing
summary: The EHT ring is the strong-deflection limit of lensing. Rays with impact parameters near b_c=√27 GM/c² wind around the photon sphere, forming the shadow edge and nested photon subrings, each demagnified by ~e^{−π} in Schwarzschild. The same deflection law gives Einstein rings in the weak-field limit.

name: Black-hole demographics and host-galaxy scaling
summary: Nearly every massive galaxy hosts a central black hole whose mass tracks its bulge, as in the M–σ relation. Black-hole masses from horizon-scale imaging and from stellar and gas dynamics calibrate these scaling relations, from Sgr A* to M87*.
sources: Kormendy & Ho (2013). "Coevolution (Or Not) of Supermassive Black Holes and Host Galaxies". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 51, 511. [arXiv:1304.7762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7762)

name: M87*: horizon-scale image of an AGN engine
summary: The EHT image of M87*, the core of a radio-loud AGN with a kiloparsec jet, shows a ~42 μas ring that matches the Kerr shadow of a 6.5×10⁹ M_sun black hole. GRMHD accretion and jet models are scored directly against the image and its polarisation.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Sgr A*: the Galactic Centre black hole
summary: Decades of S-star orbits weigh Sgr A* at ~4×10⁶ M_sun, and in 2022 the EHT imaged it as a ~52 μas ring consistent with a Kerr shadow. The two methods give independent mass-to-distance ratios, and they agree.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2022). "First Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole in the Center of the Milky Way". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 930, L12. [doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ac6674](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac6674)

Ghez et al. (2008). "Measuring Distance and Properties of the Milky Way's Central Supermassive Black Hole with Stellar Orbits". *Astrophys. J.* 689, 1044. [arXiv:0808.2870](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2870)

name: de Sitter horizon thermodynamics
summary: In a Λ-dominated universe each observer has a cosmological event horizon with the Gibbons–Hawking temperature ħH/(2πk_B) and an area entropy, obeying the same laws as black-hole horizons. For our H₀ this gives T~10⁻³⁰ K and S~10¹²² k_B, the maximum entropy of the observable universe.
map: T_{\rm dS}=\frac{\hbar H}{2\pi k_B},\quad S_{\rm dS}=\frac{k_BA}{4\ell_P^2}=\frac{\pi k_Bc^5}{G\hbar H^2}

name: Hawking evaporation bounds primordial-black-hole DM
summary: Primordial black holes lighter than ~5×10¹¹ kg would have evaporated by today, and slightly heavier ones would still emit Hawking gamma rays and e±. Gamma-ray, 511 keV-line and CMB data therefore exclude PBHs as all of the dark matter below ~10¹⁴ kg, leaving the asteroid-mass window open.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Black-hole superradiance constrains ultralight bosons
summary: Bosons whose Compton wavelength is comparable to a Kerr black hole's size form gravitational 'atoms' that grow by superradiance while ω<mΩ_H, draining the hole's spin. Measured spins of stellar and supermassive black holes exclude some ultralight-boson mass ranges, and the clouds should emit monochromatic gravitational waves.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)

name: ISCO sets the radiative efficiency of accretion
summary: A thin accretion disk radiates the binding energy at the innermost stable circular orbit. Its efficiency η=1−E_ISCO rises from 5.7% for Schwarzschild (r=6GM/c²) to 42% for maximal prograde Kerr. Soltan's argument, comparing integrated quasar light with the relic SMBH mass density, uses η to infer typical spins.

name: Cosmology is GR applied to the whole universe
summary: Modern cosmology is general relativity with a homogeneous, isotropic source. The Einstein equations with Λ and the FLRW ansatz give the Friedmann equations that ΛCDM fits to CMB, BAO and supernova data, so every cosmological test is also a large-scale test of GR.
map:

u}+\Lambda g_{\mu
u}= rac{8\pi G}{c^4}T_{\mu
u}\Rightarrow H^2= rac{8\pi G}{3}ho- rac{kc^2}{a^2}+ rac{\Lambda c^2}{3}
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)
Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: TOV equation and the neutron-star maximum mass
summary: Relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium, the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equation from the Einstein equations with a perfect-fluid source, sets neutron-star structure. Because pressure itself gravitates, every equation of state has a maximum mass, and the Buchdahl bound caps compactness at 2GM/(Rc²) < 8/9.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)

name: Structure growth from linearised Einstein equations
summary: Cosmological perturbation theory is the Einstein equations linearised about FLRW. In Newtonian gauge the 00 component gives a Poisson equation for the Bardeen potential, and sub-horizon matter obeys a growth equation whose solution D(a) and growth rate f≈Ω_m^{0.55} are what BAO and RSD surveys measure.
sources: Eisenstein et al. (2005). "Detection of the Baryon Acoustic Peak in the Large-Scale Correlation Function of SDSS Luminous Red Galaxies". *Astrophys. J.* 633, 560. [arXiv:astro-ph/0501171](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0501171)

name: FLRW metric: the exact solution behind expansion
summary: The Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker metric is the exact solution for a homogeneous, isotropic universe, and de Sitter is its Λ-dominated limit. Its scale factor a(t) defines redshift, the distance measures and the expansion history H(z) that cosmology fits.

name: Dark energy or modified gravity?
summary: Cosmic acceleration can sit on the right side of Einstein's equations, as a dark-energy fluid with w≈−1, or on the left, as f(R), Horndeski or massive gravity. The two are degenerate in H(z) and are told apart by the growth of structure and lensing; any modification must also be screened to pass Solar-System tests.
sources: Sotiriou & Faraoni (2010). "f(R) theories of gravity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 451. [arXiv:0805.1726](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1726)

name: Gravitational slip: lensing vs dynamics tests GR
summary: Light responds to Φ+Ψ, while galaxies and peculiar velocities respond to Ψ alone. GR without anisotropic stress requires Φ=Ψ, so combining weak lensing with redshift-space distortions (the E_G statistic, slip η, μ–Σ parametrisations) tests modified gravity on Mpc–Gpc scales.

name: Starobinsky R² inflation is f(R) gravity
summary: The action f(R)=R+R²/(6M²) is conformally equivalent to GR plus a scalar field with a plateau potential. It drives inflation with n_s≈1−2/N and r≈12/N², inside Planck's preferred region, so the earliest successful inflation model is a modified-gravity theory.
sources: Starobinsky (1980). "A new type of isotropic cosmological models without singularity". *Phys. Lett. B* 91, 99. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X)
Sotiriou & Faraoni (2010). "f(R) theories of gravity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 451. [arXiv:0805.1726](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1726)

name: MOND needs a relativistic modified-gravity completion
summary: MOND modifies Newtonian dynamics below a₀≈1.2×10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻². To predict lensing and the CMB it needs a relativistic completion such as TeVeS or AeST, which places it among scalar–vector–tensor modified-gravity theories. GW170817 falsified the original TeVeS, which had gravitons and photons travelling on different metrics.
sources: Milgrom (1983). "A modification of the Newtonian dynamics as a possible alternative to the hidden mass hypothesis". *Astrophys. J.* 270, 365. [doi:10.1086/161130](https://doi.org/10.1086/161130)

name: GW170817's speed of gravity prunes dark-energy models
summary: The 1.7 s delay between GW170817 and GRB 170817A over ~40 Mpc fixes the speed of gravity to within ~10⁻¹⁵ of c. That eliminates the Horndeski and beyond-Horndeski dark-energy models whose tensor speed differs from c on cosmological backgrounds, including quartic and quintic galileons.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)

name: Light deflection: from 1919 eclipse to lensing
summary: The GR deflection angle 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value and weighted by the PPN factor (1+γ)/2, is the kernel of the lens equation. The 1919 eclipse test grew into Einstein rings, cosmic shear and time-delay cosmography, and comparing lensing with dynamics tests γ on galactic scales.
sources: Dyson, Eddington & Davidson (1920). "A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field, from Observations Made at the Total Eclipse of May 29, 1919". *Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A* 220, 291. [doi:10.1098/rsta.1920.0009](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1920.0009)

name: S2's orbit tests GR near Sgr A*
summary: Adaptive-optics astrometry and spectroscopy of the star S2 detected the combined gravitational redshift and transverse Doppler shift at its 2018 pericentre, and later the prograde Schwarzschild precession of its orbit. This carries tests of GR to the potential of a 4×10⁶ M_sun black hole.
sources: GRAVITY Collaboration (2018). "Detection of the gravitational redshift in the orbit of the star S2 near the Galactic centre massive black hole". *Astron. Astrophys.* 615, L15. [arXiv:1807.09409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.09409)

name: Solar-System ephemerides as tests of GR
summary: Mercury's anomalous 43″ per century perihelion advance was GR's first success. Modern planetary ephemerides, built from radar, spacecraft tracking and lunar laser ranging, must include 1PN terms, and their fits bound the PPN parameters β and γ to ~10⁻⁵ along with the Nordtvedt effect and Ġ/G.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Binary pulsars: strong-field GR laboratories
summary: Pulsars in tight binaries, such as the Hulse–Taylor system and the Double Pulsar, yield post-Keplerian parameters: periastron advance, Shapiro delay and orbital decay. These test GR's quadrupole formula to better than 0.1% and weigh neutron stars, including the ~2 M_sun Shapiro-delay masses that constrain the equation of state.
sources: Hulse & Taylor (1975). "Discovery of a pulsar in a binary system". *Astrophys. J.* 195, L51. [doi:10.1086/181708](https://doi.org/10.1086/181708)

name: Solar oblateness and the perihelion test
summary: The Sun's quadrupole J₂ also advances Mercury's perihelion. Dicke and Goldenberg's 1967 oblateness claim (J₂~2.5×10⁻⁵) would have spoiled GR's 43″ and favoured Brans–Dicke theory. Helioseismic inversions of solar rotation later fixed J₂≈2.2×10⁻⁷, a negligible correction.
sources: Christensen-Dalsgaard (2002). "Helioseismology". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1073. [arXiv:astro-ph/0207403](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0207403)
Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Standard sirens: H₀ without a distance ladder
summary: A compact-binary waveform gives the luminosity distance directly from its amplitude and chirp, with no distance-ladder calibration. With a host-galaxy redshift, GW170817 gave H₀=70^{+12}_{−8} km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹. Tens to hundreds of sirens could become an independent arbiter of the Hubble tension.
sources: Abbott et al. (2017). "A gravitational-wave standard siren measurement of the Hubble constant". *Nature* 551, 85. [arXiv:1710.05835](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05835)

name: Compact mergers as high-energy engines
summary: The compact-object mergers that GW detectors see also produce short GRBs and kilonovae, and are candidate sources of neutrinos and cosmic rays. GW triggers therefore drive joint searches with gamma-ray, X-ray and neutrino observatories.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)

name: GW170817 opened GW multi-messenger astronomy
summary: The binary-neutron-star merger GW170817 was followed 1.7 s later by GRB 170817A and then by a kilonova across the spectrum. This one event confirmed that neutron-star mergers make short GRBs and produce r-process elements.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
LIGO, Virgo et al. (2017). "Multi-messenger Observations of a Binary Neutron Star Merger". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L12. [arXiv:1710.05833](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05833)

name: Pair-instability gap in the BH mass spectrum
summary: Stellar evolution predicts few black holes between ~50 and ~130 M_sun, because pair-instability supernovae disrupt helium cores in that range. GW catalogues test this prediction. GW190521's ~85 M_sun component lies inside the gap, pointing to hierarchical mergers or uncertain ¹²C(α,γ) rates.
sources: Woosley, Heger & Weaver (2002). "The evolution and explosion of massive stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1015. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015)

name: Primordial gravitational waves and CMB B-modes
summary: Tensor perturbations, the gravitational waves from inflation, create a quadrupolar anisotropy at last scattering. Thomson scattering turns it into curl-type B-mode polarisation, which scalar modes cannot make at linear order. The tensor-to-scalar ratio is bounded to r<0.036, and lensing B-modes are the main foreground.

name: GW alerts and sky localisation for follow-up
summary: A three-detector LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA network triangulates a merger from arrival-time differences and issues low-latency alerts. GW170817's 28 deg² error region let optical telescopes find its kilonova in NGC 4993 within 11 hours.
sources: LIGO, Virgo et al. (2017). "Multi-messenger Observations of a Binary Neutron Star Merger". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L12. [arXiv:1710.05833](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05833)

name: Binary-evolution channels behind GW mergers
summary: Isolated binary evolution (mass transfer, common envelope, supernova kicks) and dynamical assembly in clusters predict different merger rates, mass ratios and spin–orbit alignments. GW catalogues weigh these channels through rates and effective spins. The Peters inspiral time sets which binaries merge within a Hubble time.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Tidal deformability measures neutron-star radii
summary: In a neutron-star inspiral the tidal Love number enters the GW phase at 5PN order. GW170817 bounded the tidal deformability of a 1.4 M_sun star to Λ≲800, implying radii of ~11–13 km and ruling out the stiffest nuclear equations of state.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
